text:
inc-bot: Pager triggered: Elevated 5xx + streaming disconnects on api.streaming.prod (alert: STREAMING_ERR_RATE > 5% for 3m). Incident #INV-2026 created. Priority: P1

alice.eng-oncall: Acked. I'm on it. Quick snapshot: 5xx spike started ~1825072000, coincides with higher request rate from a few large customers. Streaming disconnects + chunked-encoding 502s.

maria.runtime: Seeing a pattern: gateway shows a lot of `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `chunked encoding: unexpected EOF` from our runtime pool. KV cache hit rates look normal.

dan.sre: Any recent deploys?

alice.eng-oncall: No user-facing deploys in prod since yesterday. infra autoscaler bumped capacity around 1825071000 but nothing that should affect chunked responses.

kevin.support: Multiple customers reported aborted streams and partial responses; one customer reported repeated reconnects and duplicate tokens billed. Customer impact estimate: ~8-12% of streaming sessions for the last 20m, highest in eu-west-1.

maria.runtime: Attaching sample proxy logs (head):

```
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] upstream 10.2.3.54: read() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] client 10.10.5.9:52234 chunked encoding: premature end of data
[2026-03-12T14:07:12Z] upstream sent invalid header while reading response header from upstream
```

maria.runtime: And runtime logs from the serving instance: `ERROR stream_writer: failed to flush chunked buffer: BrokenPipeError` repeated.

dan.sre: Could be backpressure causing fast-kill of connection. We should check ktps (tokens/sec) spikes and per-connection memory limits. Also check gateway timeout/keepalive settings.

alice.eng-oncall: I can try increasing gateway keepalive and proxy buffer sizes on a small canary set. Plan: 1) enable increased keepalive + proxy buffer on 2 nodes in eu-west-1; 2) temporarily route ~10% of streaming traffic through fallback tier with slightly coarser batching (model-variant: gpt-medium-fallback) to reduce per-connection pressure; 3) monitor error rates, latencies, and token billing. Anyone object?

liz.product: Need to notify affected customers with ETA and mitigation. Kept short: "We're seeing intermittent streaming disconnects; temporary mitigation in progress; we'll follow up with root cause."

kevin.support: I'll draft a message. Also flagging a high-volume partner (partner-acme) for immediate outreach.

maria.runtime: Before we change routing, one more data point: host metrics show that the runtime process enters a state with CPU locked at ~90% and write syscall latency climbs, coincident with chunk flush failures. Suggests inability to keep up with streaming writes.

alice.eng-oncall: Initiating live mitigation: starting canary config change now (node ids: i-0a1b2c3d4e, i-0f1e2d3c4b). I'll post results.

ops-bot: Deploy job started: change/proxy-buffer-and-keepalive (canary) by alice.eng-oncall.

alice.eng-oncall: Canary done. No immediate errors on canary nodes, streams stay open longer (prelim). Error rate for canary dropped from 7.2% -> 1.1% over 2m. Rolling to additional 6 nodes.

maria.runtime: Rolling looks good so far. Error rate cluster-wide falling from 8.9% -> 3.4% after 50% rollout. However, some customers still show reconnects — likely they hit older edge nodes or upstream proxies.

dan.sre: Start fallback routing to reduce pressure on busy runtime pool. ops-bot: execute roll traffic rule to route 10% streaming sessions to model-variant gpt-medium-fallback.

ops-bot: Traffic rule applied.

kevin.support: Noting billing concern: customers on fallback will see slightly lower token fidelity; make sure support message includes that.

liz.product: Agreed. Provide opt-in line: "If you need uninterrupted high-fidelity streams, we recommend retry logic with exponential backoff — we are restoring capacity now."

maria.runtime: Side investigation: observed increased client-initiated cancellations around the same timestamps (client cancel followed by immediate reconnect). Hypothesis: some client SDKs may be aggressively retrying when they see slow first-byte, causing hammering and amplifying pressure.

alice.eng-oncall: Can we capture a few full connection traces from the gateway to see timing? Enable debug trace for 60s on 3 nodes.

maria.runtime: Traces enabled. Sample trace: connect -> initial-token 0.8s -> initial chunk delay 1.6s -> client abort after 2s -> reconnect 0.1s later -> repeated. That's exactly the retry loop.

dan.sre: That matches a vicious cycle: slow MTTR -> client retries -> more concurrency -> more slow writes -> more retries. Mitigation: 1) adjust client-facing timeout recommendations, 2) throttle retry rate at gateway for suspicious clients, 3) add short jitter on reconnect backoff guidance.

alice.eng-oncall: Implementing a short-term gateway throttle: limit per-IP simultaneous streaming connections to 8 and add token-bucket rate limit for new stream creation. Applying in eu-west-1 now.

ops-bot: Config change applied: streaming-conn-limit=8, stream-create-ratelimit=20/min per IP

kevin.support: Noted. Support message updated to encourage SDK patch that backoff-retries.

liz.product: I'll prepare a status update for customers: brief incident summary, mitigation steps taken, expected follow-up.

maria.runtime: Observed metrics after both mitigations: global error rate down to 1.9%, streaming disconnects reduced by ~75%, client cancellation spike down. Write syscall latency normalized.

alice.eng-oncall: Good progress. Moving to recovery state. Next: collect flame graphs and heap/disk stats from affected runtime instances for postmortem. Assigning follow-ups:
- maria.runtime: collect traces + logs for 20 affected instances and annotate with timeline.
- dan.sre: validate autoscaler behavior and whether scaling contributed to transient pressure.
- alice.eng-oncall: produce incident timeline and coordinate customer comms with liz/kevin.

ops-bot: Incident #INV-2026 status -> mitigation in place, monitoring.

kevin.support: Draft sent to affected customers (partners flagged).

liz.product: Sending customer bulletin now.

alice.eng-oncall: Closing pager on-call. Handoff: dan.sre is primary for postmortem and further checks. dan, you're oncall for followups.

dan.sre: Taking handoff. I'll run memory/IO profiles overnight and convene root cause meeting in 4 hours. If regressions occur, ping me directly and reopen incident. :thumbsup:

inc-bot: Incident #INV-2026 moved to MONITORING. Notes: mitigations applied (proxy keepalive+buffers, gateway throttles, traffic fallback), customer impact ~8-12% sessions at peak, now reduced to ~1.9% error rate.

alice.eng-oncall: Thanks team. Saving logs to /var/lib/incidents/INV-2026/ and will attach to the final postmortem.

maria.runtime: One last note for the postmortem: look at the interaction of write syscall latency with chunked transfer buffer size; we may want to tune runtime flush thresholds to avoid head-of-line stalls.

kevin.support: I'll follow up with customers in 2 hours with RCA when available.

(incident timeline entries and attachments were uploaded to the incident tracker)

inc-bot: Incident #INV-2026 resolved at 1825074300 (status: mitigated; awaiting postmortem).
